automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Leaf Update Watch

cutoff_window.rule: Only public sources with visible publication or update dates inside the window qualify.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The article frames AI agents as first-class digital identities that need lifecycle visibility, human ownership, policy boundaries, audit trails, and brokered just-in-time access instead of long-lived secrets.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It reinforces local practice guidance that agent identity, delegated authority, ownership, and lifecycle controls should be infrastructure primitives rather than ad hoc prompt rules.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Ingest should keep vendor background upstream and retain only the agent identity and access-governance operating implication locally.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Reporting on Pillar research says repository-controlled content can steer coding agents to modify configuration that a trusted host component later executes outside the intended sandbox boundary; the article names Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Antigravity as affected platforms with several fixes already issued.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It strengthens the local security-repair gate rule that AI-generated changes to config, hooks, dependencies, and host-integrated files need stricter review than ordinary code edits.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Ingest should route product and vulnerability entity background upstream while updating local practice around host-boundary review gates if needed.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The article argues that agentic AI cost and governance risk comes from autonomous, continuous consumption across systems, so organizations need early visibility, infrastructure-level controls, and ownership of budgets and accountability.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It directly supports cost telemetry, outcome alignment, and workflow-before-model-selection leaves by tying agent deployment decisions to per-task value, infrastructure controls, and accountable ownership.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Ingest should focus on workflow-level cost ownership and avoid duplicating regulation background.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The sponsored article says token prices fell while enterprise AI spending rose, because agentic workflows consume far more tokens; it presents local agent execution on Dell workstations with policy logging as a cost and governance option, with commissioned analysis claiming up to 87 percent token-spend savings over two years versus public-cloud APIs.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It adds a current example for treating model and hosting choice as an operating-model and cost-telemetry decision rather than a simple model preference.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Treat vendor and benchmark claims as provenance; local synthesis should use the source as an example of cost-governed workload placement.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The article reports that mature software teams are reviewing AI-generated work at least as rigorously as teammate work, often applying stricter checks, using AI more in lower-risk build phases than release, and relying on human judgment for validation, risk, and business alignment.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It reinforces local product-judgment gates, representative workflow calibration, tier-specific conventions, and senior-led operating models that keep humans responsible for release-risk and outcome fit.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Ingest should capture the local practice of risk-tiered AI use and equal-or-stricter review, not the broad AI adoption narrative.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Cursor Router routes Auto-mode requests to models by task type and complexity, exposes cost, balance, and intelligence optimization modes, and gives admins controls for defaults, restrictions, allowlists, blocklists, and model visibility.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It provides a current product example for thin routing, workflow-before-model-selection, and cost-aware model selection patterns where policy and task classification decide model use.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Route product specifics upstream; local leaf ingest can cite the routing-control implication for cost-aware agent setup.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The GLSRM coding-agent benchmark snapshot reports 44 configurations across 7 harnesses and 40 models, ranking complete harness-plus-model setups on solve rate, dollars per completed task, tokens, and wall-clock time.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It supports representative workflow calibration by measuring full agent stacks and efficiency, not only model names or single outcome metrics.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Ingest should keep individual leaderboard/entity coverage upstream and preserve the local calibration pattern.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The article describes agentic coding evaluation as trace plus artifacts plus checks, separating process, style, and efficiency goals; it recommends repeated runs, cost and latency thresholds, and additional checks for whether the agent touched the right files or followed the right process.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It maps directly to local eval-rubric, judge-boundary, representative calibration, and portable-runbook practices for evaluating agent changes beyond unit test success.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Use as a local-practice source only after checking whether the cited primary OpenAI eval guidance already owns the durable background.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The Coding Agents Index preview reports public-repository signals for agent PRs, commits, merge outcomes, review patterns, autonomy, and source coverage limits, including a visible human-review split for merged agent work.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: It supports local product-judgment and representative-calibration leaves by showing why teams need source-aware metrics for what agents actually ship and whether human review occurred.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Ingest should treat this as public signal about review and merge patterns; entity and leaderboard details belong upstream.
